column1: # The Phijets drawn as the house's letters and cards are built: straight
# lines and circles, nothing drawn by hand (the user, 24 November 2026:
# "on the font and different radii only, not artist curves but geometric
# ones"). Read by script/jet.py, which writes the outlines (jet-*.svg)
# and the jets' body and window rows of thing.tsv.
# Every outline is a chain of circles taken with the clock (y runs
# down), each joined to the next by the line that touches both, as a
# letter's round corners are joined by its straight strokes:
#   point  x y        a corner cut sharp
#   round  x y r      a corner rounded outward
#   hollow x y r      a corner rounded inward
#   on     x y r h    the point of circle (x y r) at height h, its front
#   pill   x0 y0 x1 y1  a pill: its ends half its width round
# Lengths are shares of R, the nose's radius, which is the body's
# height: every other radius is a share of it (1/4, 1/8), as a card's
# parts take shares of the theme's corner. An opening set inside the
# body keeps the body's centre and gives up the inset from its radius,
# as an inner card does inside its card. `size` is the length and the
# width in metres; y 0 is the keel.
# Where every body stands, and how round its edge is: the keel this high
# in metres, the edge round by this share of the body's height (less than
# an opening's inset of 1/8 R in 3/2 R, so every opening stays on the
# flat), a window's edge by this share of its own.
# The long jet: the nose a quarter of a circle the body's height, cut
# sharp at the keel; a flat roof; the tail's back one upright stroke, its
# foot and its fin's top round by a quarter; the fin's front swept down
# into the roof through a hollow of a quarter.
